utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everybody in the courtroom and to those who are listening to our procedures. If there are no procedural matters, the witness should be brought in, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Janc. Welcome back to the courtroom. I have again to remind you that the affirmation to tell the truth still applies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye is conducting his re-direct. Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good afternoon to you, Your Honours; good afternoon everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And good afternoon to you, Mr. Janc. I have just a few topics that I'd like to cover with you in the re-direct examination, following the testimony on Thursday last. Let me start, if I could, but putting up P170. This is your report from 21 April 2010.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And we'll need to go to page 5 in the English; 6 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And what we have on the screen, and hopefully we'll have the B/C/S up in a minute, is the third page of the tables you have concerning the total numbers, as you've indicated have identified individuals. And here we can see the numbers in two columns which represent the figures that you obtained for March 2009 and February 2010, respectively.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, you should wait until the B/C/S version is appearing on the screen. It's not there.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Is this the right page you were asking for?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: It is Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: In these two columns, we can see the total figures that you have represented here. On the left, would be the numbers that were -- that you determined as of March 2009, and on the far right, the numbers you determined as of February 2010. Does that sound right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: During the course of your cross-examination, you made reference to identified individuals. And I just want to make sure that we're clear on what that means in the context of your report. So if you would, could you tell us what you mean when you say "identified individuals" in the course of your testimony and also as indicated in this report?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It would be helpful if the relevant part could be enlarged in both languages, especially in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, perhaps we go to second page of my report, and you -- we can find the term of identified individual in a footnote number 4. So it would be second page of my report. Actually, footnote number 3, where I say that: "Identified means an individual with a unique DNA profile whether with or without a name." So we can see the footnote number 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Is that how you used the term during the course of your testimony, during cross-examination and direct examination, for that matter?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You were asked at transcript page 14.683, I have here lines 21 through 14.684, line 10, by General Tolimir the following: "Thank you, Mr. Janc, and all those 5.777," if we can go back to pages 5 and 6, respectively, we'll see that number, "all those 5.777 that were buried in graves, do you consider all of them as having been killed outside of combat? Thank you." And your answer was: "Yes. I think that I already answered that most of them, if not all of them, were, indeed, killed or executed. Why I am saying 'most, if not all,' I can explain because here Glogova is the big issue because we know that most of them there, again, are the victims from the Kravica execution. Apart from that, we also know that some bodies were taken from other locations which were picked up along the road, the Konjevic Polje-Bratunac road. I think a victim testified here about this procedure going on, and so those were also brought into the same grave and for those victims which were, according to this individual, around 15 or 30 of them in total, we can't say if they were killed in combat or were executed. That's why I'm saying most of them, if not all of them, are victims of the execution in these graves -- in these mass graves." Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Does this number, 5.777, also include, therefore, individuals that were part of the surface remain totals that you found that you considered to be victims of executions?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are asking now specifically for these bodies which were picked up along Konjevic Polje-Bratunac road or in general?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: In general.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Those are only victims from the graves. Those found on the surface, we have another figure which is 703 which is the one figure under this 5777 on my chart.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now the number that you have here, 703, does that include the number of the total surface remains or surface remains cases or the total number of identified individuals that were recovered from the surface?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the number for the total number of individuals identified.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: So it doesn't -- does it include what you might consider a unique DNA profile as you've indicated before, for which a name has not been yet ascertained?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. For surface remains -- remains, I didn't include the unique profiles.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. So this is just the people that have names that are recovered from the surface, matched through DNA analysis; is that fair?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You indicated at transcript page 14.687, and this was during your discussion on cross-examination concerning surface remains recovered in the Pobudje area. The question is as follows and then I'll give the answer: "Thank you. After this, I'm not sure at all what is in your report and what is in Mr. Ruez's report, can you please tell us in one sentence whether these 600 bodies were found, and, if not, how many of the bodies examined by the Finnish team were found? Can you please tell us the exact number. Thank you." And you answer is: "Okay. By the Finnish team, 30 bodies have been picked up, collected from the ground in 1996. In addition, that same year around 250 bodies have been collected by the BH, so we have 300 bodies, or body parts or whatever, so 300, throughout the year. So it means from 1996 up until the end of 2009, additional surface remains were collected from this area."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Please slow down when reading.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, I'll do: "... additional surface remains were collected from this area and that's why in my report, the total number is 558 so far identified, so it means the bodies which were collected from this area from 1996 up until the end of 2009. When the Finnish team was there in 1996, only about 300 bodies were collected at that time, so in addition, we now have double number so because I already emphasised several times that this number is growing over the years, so I hope I made myself much clearer now." What I'd like to do is to go to - hopefully - the relevant page in your report. Just a moment. We're going to need to go to page 43 in the English, 60 in the B/C/S, just to identify the section of the report we're talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What we have here is Appendix B to your report and you can see that it's the -- the caption is it discusses the surface remains. You have four categories and peers in the middle of the page, and we'll have to go to the next page in the B/C/S to see them. You've identified the Pobudje area, Baljkovica area, Snagovo area, and other areas. If we go to the next page in English and we might have to go to the next page in the B/C/S, I'm not sure just now. But we can see the total number here of the 558. We'll go to the next page in the B/C/S, page 62 for the record. And you've indicated here these 558 individuals. Are these again the total number of surface remain cases or the total number of identified, meaning a name attached to the remains, surface remain cases?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are again the total number of the identified individuals.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And as of the writing of this report, how many surface-remain cases identified or -- that is, DNA-identified with a name or without as an individual DNA profiles had been obtained, how many cases were there in total?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So you can find the figure one page before we have on the screen now, and you will see that in total 961 surface remains cases were collected so far.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. I'd like to show you, since you refer to it your cross-examination, 65 ter 7413.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think this might be an exhibit that was not originally on the Prosecution's 65 ter list. It is, though, the Finnish team report that Mr. Janc expressly referred to in his cross-examination. I would move to add it at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, any objections?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we have not seen it, so I don't know what I would object to, when I haven't seen it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The question was if you have objection to add this document to this -- the 65 ter exhibit list of the Prosecution so that he can use it in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. But, as for objections, I cannot raise objections against something I have never seen in my life, thank you, as there is no translation into Serbian or anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I take it there is no objection and at the moment we are not dealing with receiving it into evidence. It may be -- leave is granted to add it to the 65 ter exhibit list. Please continue, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. We do not have a B/C/S translation of this document as yet. So I'll read a bit of it into the record so General Tolimir can familiarise himself with what it is or has at least a pretty basic understanding of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, first of all, do you recognise this report?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: For the record, it is entitled, "Report of the Finnish Forensic Expert Team," and it is dated 8 July 1997.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, is this the report that you refer to during the course of your testimony on Thursday last, the 26th?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct. This is the one.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. If we could go to the next page, please, in the English. I'm sorry, we'll go to the following page after this. You will see in the next-to-last paragraph, let me just read the last -- the third to last paragraph so General Tolimir has the sense of what this is about. The third last to paragraph reads: "The Finnish ministry of foreign affairs was several times in contact with Justice Richard Goldstone and Mr. Graham Blewitt of the ICTY to inform the Tribunal of the results of the Finnish experts and to co-ordinate with the Tribunal's own efforts to exhume mortal remains from mass graves in the vicinity. It was not possible for the ICTY however to send observer to follow the field-work of the Finnish expert team in Kravica." First, the reference here to Kravica, does this refer to the Pobudje area that you were discussing during the cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct. This is area behind Kravica warehouse.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: In the following paragraph, that is the next to last, it says that the 30 sets of human remains actually recovered in the field in 1996 proved somewhat less than the expected -- projected, I'm sorry, 40 to 60 bodies envisaged in the project plan of 30 May 1996. It should be mentioned however that a number of the corpses sighted in the field had to be left where they were, because of the adverse attitude of the Pale authorities? Is this the 30 cases that you referred to during your cross-examination on Thursday?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did you take this report into account and into consideration when you arrived or determined the numbers -- the total number of surface remains that you've indicated at?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would ask Mr. Vanderpuye to clarify whether, on page 8 in line 24, 630, mortal surface remains are mentioned or only 40. Thank you. Because is he asking only about 40.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes. I do see that in the transcript and that is a mistranscription. What the text reads is 40 to 60 bodies envisaged in the project plan. 40 to 60.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you for that clarification. Thank you, Mr. Tolimir. Please carry on, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I don't think I have an answer yet to my question, which is whether or not you, Mr. Janc, took this report and these numbers into consideration in developing your own report and your own analysis as to the number of surface remains recovered as of 2010?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't quoted this report into my report because what I was taking into consideration and what numbers were used for my report were simply the identified individuals which I could find on the ICMP identification list. In addition to that, I also used the tables and documents and information provided to me by the BiH commission on missing person in relation to these surface remains. I have to admit that I read this report for my first time just recently when this issue about what Investigator Ruez testified here, and that's why I came across this report and I also read this report and I found it that this report is not contradicting my report at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you know if this report or the activities of the Finnish experts is referred to the BH documents that you relied on in your own report?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, actually, it's not. And what they provided to me was just the actual number on how many cases they have collected from the surface and how many individuals have been identified so far. So just the numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Let me show you then P20 --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, I would like to tender this Finnish report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I don't see any objection. It will be marked for identification, pending translation.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour 65 ter document 7413 shall be assigned Exhibit P2244, marked for identification, pending translation. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. I'd like to show the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can Mr. Vanderpuye please clarify whether this is a report from the Pobudje area or from the Bare area, or the Finnish forensic experts as they worked in both of these locations. So can he please specify from which one this is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. What I read into the record before referred to the activities of the Finnish expert team in Kravica. And this, I believe, the witness just testified, was the area behind the Kravica -- or behind Kravica which he has indicated as Pobudje.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I think I asked to show the witness P2076, 2076.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And while that is loading, just let me ask this. You were asked or do you remember being asked at page 14688 through 14689 questions concerning the estimate, as you mentioned, or, rather, the number provided by Jean-Rene Ruez during his testimony on 14th March 2000 of about 600 bodies recovered from this area? Surface remains, I mean.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember these questions.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could Mr. Vanderpuye please say for the record which area this concerns, because it is indefinite as it is. Can we just specify geographically what were the surface remains that Mr. Ruez was talking it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, you said "from this area." What are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, I think maybe it is best if I just read it from the transcript and hopefully that will make it clearer. At page 14.687, rather -86 in the middle of the page, General Tolimir asked the following question: "My question is the number which Mr. Ruez mentions is smaller for 80 than the one you mentioned in your report as the number of 688, so the smaller number --or the number is smaller for 80. My question is this: Did the persons whose mortal remains were found in the Bare village identified by DNA analysis? And then there's a long answer by Mr. Janc where he indicates that the Bare area is the area behind Kravica warehouse, and he says: "In that area, 558 individuals have been identified. The number that you referred to as 688 is the total number of surface remains. But as I discussed in my report, I emphasised that I categorise surface remains in three different areas," and he says, "and in Pobudje area there is only -- there is, so far, 558 individuals." This all goes into a whole long discussion about the matter. But does that help clarify the area to which these numbers relate to you, Mr. Janc?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we are all the time talking about, as I referred to Pobudje area, which is stretching from south -- from Bratunac up to Konjevic Polje. These are the hills where the most surface remains have been collected, including the area behind Kravica warehouse and Bare area.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And is your understanding that Mr. Ruez's testimony concerning the 600 bodies recovered from the surface back in 2000, his testimony was in 2000 -- is it your understanding that that number relates to that specific area or is it broader than that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is my understanding that he was referring to this area. But for more than that, you would need to clarify directly with him, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. I think I was about to show you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, could Mr. Vanderpuye clarify where the village of Bare is that Mr. Ruez referred to? Perhaps he should clarify that with the witness first and then we'll see whether it is in the general area of Brdo and Pobudje or on a specific location. Mr. Ruez specified the satellite co-ordinates.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I think that the area that Mr. Janc is referring to, as concerns Mr. Ruez's testimony, is clear on the record. I asked him specifically what is the area of -- or where is Bare village and he described it for the record, so I don't see any need for further clarification. If General Tolimir wants to explore the satellite co-ordinates or GPS co-ordinates with Mr. Janc, I think that is appropriate. If he wants to do that with leave of the Court, but I just don't see where that fits in, in terms of clarifying the record for the purposes of re-direct examination. I should point out that the area, and concerning Mr. Ruez's testimony, in particular, that was brought out just about a year ago when Mr. Tolimir testified -- Tolimir began his cross-examination of Mr. Janc and again on Thursday. So if there's any ambiguity as to that area, I think Mr. Janc's answer just a moment ago makes it quite clear what he is talking about and what he understands Mr. Ruez's testimony to refer to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, you had the opportunity to put your questions to the witness during the course of the cross-examination. Now Mr. Vanderpuye is conducting his re-examination. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, during my examination, I said that this amounted to a revision of Mr. Ruez's testimony. It now turns out that the village is somewhere up in the mountains, but Ruez said it was precisely in the village of Bare. I simply wanted him to clarify that with the witness, where the village of Bare is. Otherwise, we'll just be referring to a general area. If that is of no interest to the Court, then I don't have an interest in it either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: At the end of the day, we all have to review the different testimonies of all the witnesses of Mr. Ruez, of Mr. Janc. Of course, that is necessary. Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Once again, I was just about to show the witness P2076. All right. What we have here, Mr. Janc, is a document that was provided by the authorities of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and it concerns information regarding surface remains. Do you recall referring to this report -- or this document, I should say, during the course of your testimony on Thursday?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And if we can go to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I think it's page 3 in the B/C/S. [Microphone not activated]... English, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And what we have here is some figures concerning the collection of surface remains. Could you just briefly, first of all, confirm if this is the -- or some of the information that you relied on in generating your own report concerning the recovery of surface remains?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And could you explain to us what this shows. We have here the year of exhumation, which I think goes without saying, and then we have instances of collection from the surface and then we have number of identified persons collected from the surface. What is meant here by instances of collection from the surface?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is the table we were provided by the BiH commission on missing persons, as you can see, at the end of 2007, when we requested if the information on how many surface remains have been collected so far in relation to Srebrenica events, and this is the table they provided. And we can see in the first column on the left-hand side we have the year within this -- that many surface remains have been collected. So -- and then the second column, we have the number of cases, how many such body parts have been collected from the ground. And the last column represent how many individuals have been so far, at that time, already identified out of the surface remains from the middle column. And we can see, for example, in 1996, 213 surface remains case have been collected, and then it goes on up until 2007. In total, 877 cases collected. In addition to that, we can see the column Finnish team in 1996 collected 52 such cases. And then we have the total number of how many surface remains case have been so far collected before I referred to the number 961, which is also included in my report, but that's because the number grew in 2008 and 2009 to that many surface remains cases collected from the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Where we say here, identified persons, what does that mean? Does that mean DNA-identified? Does it mean they are identified forensically? By parents? Things of that nature. Do you know, are you able to say?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For most of them, I can say that they were identified through DNA identification by the ICMP. However, we have 35 cases -- or not cases but 35 individuals which were identified before the ICMP commenced its work in 2001 and these were also included into table and also included into my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: So you maybe have to help me a little bit with my math. But as of 2000 which is when Mr. Ruez testified, this would indicate that the number of instances of the collection of surface remains adds up to about 627. Of those, 444 would have been identified by then. Does that seem, first of all, approximately right to you; and, second of all, is that consistent with Mr. Ruez's testimony as he gave it in 2000?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is right in a way, I would say. Because -- why? Because we have to, if you count all these surface remains cases collected in each year, here is the total number for first five years from 1996 to 2000 would be, indeed, 627. The problem here is that we have 183 cases collected in 2000, so it mean -- it means the whole year that many case have been collected, and we would need to go, I think, further tables to see how many cases have been collected up until the moment when Mr. Ruez testified. So it might be -- this number might be lower. In any case, it is around 600 cases and also I would like to emphasise here that this is related to all the areas not only Pobudje area, although I'm sure that most of the cases which we can see here out of those 600 have been collected in Pobudje area. There might be then additional cases collected in Snagovo and Baljkovica area. As for the identifications on the right-hand side, I would -- I can't confirm that at the time when Mr. Ruez was testifying that we already have had that many identifications. That many identifications were concluded at the time when this report was provided to us by the BiH authorities. It means by the end of 2007.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, can you help me? When you are referring to the testimony of Mr. Janc [sic] in the year 2000 -- of Mr. Ruez, sorry, in the year 2000, in which case was this testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think this was the case against General Krstic. And if I'm not mistaken, it was in April of 2000.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Your microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It would be useful for the Defence if Mr. Vanderpuye could clarify whether Mr. Ruez testified to all the victims found following the Krstic testimony or whether he testified only about the Bare location where he said that there were 627 cases of surface collection. That would be important because Mr. Janc is now addressing those surface collections in the -- through a number of years. Therefore, we are unsure what this portion refers to specifically.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Mr. President, I think General Tolimir has gotten his answer in more ways than one. One, Mr. Janc just testified that these numbers include the total number of surface remains for more than just the area of Bare which we've discussed. And he also testified before that that his understanding of what Mr. Ruez was testifying about back in 2000 concerned the area of Bare which we've now defined through the testimony of Mr. Janc as included in the area of Pobudje. So I don't -- I don't know exactly what General Tolimir's objection is, if can you call it that. I do have a document to show Mr. Janc which I think may help clarify things somewhat but certainly will explain where these surface remains were recovered over the course of the years.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Judge Nyambe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Janc, I wonder if you can clarify for me. I'm getting confused about surface remains and -- and victims of Srebrenica, as it relates to combat activities or non-combat activities. My question therefore is as follows: Do any of the surface remains you referred to in your testimony form part of the missing persons of Srebrenica, as a result of combat or non-combat? Can you make that distinction for my understanding, please? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. All the individuals which form part of my report as surface remains are the victims of Srebrenica, which means that they are on a missing list of Srebrenica. So they went missing after the fall Srebrenica, all those 588 individuals from Pobudje area and also the others. So in total, 703, including Zepa victims. So those were all on a missing list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Can you just explain further your missing lists. Were they as a result of combat activities or other deaths?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. For most of them, we know they were found in mass graves, and this is majority of them, in total 5.777 in my report. Then we have this portion of 700 individuals which were found on the surface and which I testified that for most of them, they were most probably killed in combat. Some of them we know also died from different other sources. Different other -- in different other circumstances, sorry. Like, committed suicides, then they -- they were -- they died crossing the minefields, for example, and, of course, we know also for some of them that were executed, killed. So those found on surface would include both: killed in combat and killed in other ways, illegally killed, and also those committed suicide or died of different other sources, different other -- from different other reasons, I mean.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, could Mr. Vanderpuye clarify the following: In line 16, actually, page 16, line 18, he said that Mr. Ruez had mentioned 627 persons collected in the area of Bare. And we see that Mr. Janc mentioned only 213 irrespective of the area. Ruez said that this was all done in Bare in 1996. I'm interested in how this discrepancy can be explained by Mr. Vanderpuye and Mr. Janc. If it is outside the scope of cross-examination, then they need not answer the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I think maybe there's a translation issue or General Tolimir is not -- apprehended the issue. The questions that I put to Mr. Janc are derived from General Tolimir's questions concerning Mr. Ruez's testimony as to 600 individuals' surface remains that had been recovered. As we explored on Thursday, Mr. Ruez testified in 2000. General Tolimir put a question to Mr. Janc, suggesting that the number that Mr. Ruez referred to as 600 was a number that he arrived at in 1996, to which I objected, because there was nothing in the transcript, as put to Mr. Janc of Mr. Ruez's testimony, suggesting that 600 surface remains were recovered in 1996. In so far as his testimony occurred in 2000, and he said that 600 bodies had been recovered, it seems reasonable to conclude that 600 bodies had been recovered up until the time he had testified, in the area that General Tolimir put to Mr. Janc as Bare in the form of his questions to him. So this line of questioning on re-direct examination expands upon the question of the number of individuals that were identified or indicated by Mr. Ruez as Mr. Janc has -- and how those numbers are reflected in Mr. Janc's report. So the first question is: How many did Mr. Ruez indicate, which Mr. Janc has answered; where did he indicate those people were found, which Mr. Janc has answered; what documentation is there concerning those individuals, which has been shown to Mr. Janc; whether or not Mr. Janc is incorporated or reviewed those documents in the preparation of his own report concerning those issues, which he has testified to; whether or not the individuals that -- more than 600 individuals, the location where they were recovered can be determined, which I'm just about to put to him. All of these issues I think are relatively clear and flow directly from the cross-examination of Mr. Janc on that number of individuals.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, are you satisfied by this very precise and lengthy explanation?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am satisfied, Mr. President, when I receive any explanation. But I would like to see the reference where Mr. Ruez apparently testified about all the victims that were identified before he testified here in 2010 or at the time when he testified in the Krstic case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: At the moment we have the Witness Janc and not the Witness Ruez in the courtroom. Mr. Vanderpuye was referring to the testimony of 2010 in the Krstic trial and not in this courtroom last year. I think he made it very clear. Mr. Vanderpuye, please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I was just about to show Mr. Janc 65 ter 2769A. This is the attachment to -- which is referred to in P2076, which I've just shown the witness. Oh. I will also need to add that, if I may, to the Prosecution's 65 ter list. It was not part of the original list but as you can see it is directly related to the document that I showed Mr. Janc, which is already admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I don't see any objection. And I think that would clarify even more to have this added to the 65 ter exhibit list. Leave is granted, Mr. Vanderpuye. Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President. I would note that we don't have yet an English translation of this document. But I think Mr. Janc may be able to get us through it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And what this shows, Mr. Janc, first of all, can you tell us, do you recognise this?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And what does it show?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a table which was provided along with the table we have just seen before by the BiH Federal Commission on Missing Persons at the end of 2007. And this is just the breakdown per year. So we can see here which exhumations and when and where have been conducted within the particular period of time, or on specific date. As we can see, the second column, it says the date of the exhumation conducted, and then we have the third column, we have the place of the exhumation. And the fourth column, it says the municipality of exhumation. And then we have the fifth column where it says the code, the exhumation code which was assigned to particular body, body part, or anything. And then later we have the columns where we have different numbers how many such individuals cases have been collected from the ground. And this is -- this is all relate to surface remains which were collected in that area. And we can see from the third column that most of them have been collected from Pobudje area. And also the commission is referring to these bodies as being collected from Pobudje, although we can see the exact site was Kamenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And this is for -- what we're looking at now is ERN page X018968 [sic] and that refers to the year 1996 and indicates a total number, I believe, of 213 plus 52, from the Finnish team. And for a total of 265; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. On this table, we can see the last column is referring to Finnish team exhumation with a code-name PM, and those 52 cases were collected by Finnish team.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Let's just go over to the next page --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Before we do that, we should correct the transcript. The ERN number was wrongly recorded. It should be X0189698. Thank you. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Let's take a look at the next page, 1997.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And here we have similar information. If we go to the following page, we should see the total. Here it says 159, is that right, exhumations?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, 159 cases were collected from the surface in 1997.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And that should correspond, indeed, to P2076, page 3, showing the table in English and the second page in the B/C/S which records the same number. And let's look at the next page, X018971 [sic]. And this is for 1998. And records 30 exhumations there; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct. And we can see from this table that all those exhumed are collected on a surface in 1998 were collected from Zvornik area. So those were not collected in Pobudje area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Again this is an mistake with the number. Mr. Vanderpuye, you misspoke. The last figure should be 9701. The 0 was missing. Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'm not going to go through all of them, but have you had a chance to check this against the table that I showed you, P2076 and can you confirm that the numbers and totals reflected in this attachment appear in that table.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have had the chance to review all these tables and I can confirm that they correspond.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'd like to tender 65 ter 2769A. I wondered, and this may be a question for the Registrar, whether it could be admitted under a sub-designation of P2076 because it is -- it is essentially an attachment to that document. It might be easier to find later on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I wanted to put this question to you, why you didn't tendered it with the original document?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: It's a good question. I think the answer to that is that the original document came in as a 92 ter or 92 bis exhibit, so it had already been premarked or provisionally admitted and was subsequently admitted with the testimony of Ewa Tabeau. And only part of it had been used with her in her prior testimony and not the full document which is why only part of it came in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: These sheets, the attachment to P2076, will be marked for identification, pending translation, as P2076A. Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Just to follow up on a question that was put to you by the Honourable Judge Nyambe, you were asked a question also by General Tolimir concerning how you characterise victims in your report. And what I wanted to ask you was: In relation to the surface remains that were recovered, were any of these surface remains, as per your report, or in your -- or, in your view, did you consider them as non-combat-related casualties, that is, the victims of executions the same as some individuals or all of the individuals, you've said, that were recovered from the mass graves?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct. Some of them were executed. We have evidence on them being executed.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Just so that we're clear, the transcript reference for Judge Nyambe's question, I don't have but I think we can all remember that; but for General Tolimir's questions on cross-examination, the transcript is page 14.677 and lines 14 through 22. In particular, he asked you whether or not your report was neutral in the sense of describing whether a person was killed in combat or was killed in an unlawful way. And in response, you indicated that your report presents the numbers of individuals identified from the graves, individual graves found on the surface, and you said you thought you were clear in your testimony that you confined combat casualties within the category of surface remains. So my question is really just the inverse of that, whether you can find non-combat execution-type casualties within the surface remains.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And, in particular, can you tell us to the best of your recollection whether or not you included the remains found in Godinjske Bare related to Trnovo as non-combat-related remains, victims?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are in a section others in my report, and we all know that from the video on their execution that they were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And what about executions near Snagovo? Did you include those individuals among the victims recovered from the surface?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think those individuals are found -- actually, there is one individual, if I'm not mistaken, which was found in Tisova Kosa which was found on the surface and we know that he was executed. Another one was being found in a grave which is referred to in my report as Brezeva grave.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Well, I was going to ask you about Tisova Kosa, which, as you know, in the investigation relates to what's referred to as Nezuk executions. But referring more specifically to the Snagovo executions, do you recall what grave-sites or what locations were associated with the executions of these men, approximately six of them?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I was asked this question already before, and I still don't know the answer. So I don't know, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Judge Nyambe has a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Thank you. Just now, in page 26, line 19 to 21, in answer to Mr. Vanderpuye's question, you have said as follows: "I think those individuals are found -- actually, there is one individual, if I'm not mistaken. ... which was found on the surface and we know that he was executed." Now how do you distinguish this individual, who I understand is found on the surface, among other surface remains as having been executed as opposed to maybe having died of -- having died in combat or suicide or by walking over a land-mine? How are you able to distinguish this particular individual as having been executed? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. For this particular individual, we have a statement. And also it's evidence in this case, because survive of this execution testified here, and he named this individual as being executed next to him. And he was found on the surface.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned that you had some information concerning an individual that was executed in the area of Tisova Kosa, as testimony in this case. Are you aware of any other testimony that was given with respect to this issue in this or in the Popovic case?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think in relation to this issue, to this same execution, we have two survivors and both testified in these two cases. For one, I am sure in this case. I mean, in Tolimir trial. The other, I think, testified in Popovic trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What I'd like to show you -- well, let me ask you this before I do. Did you consider the testimony of these two individuals in your characterisation of the surface remains recovered from Tisova Kosa as of non-combat -- as non-combat-related casualties?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Then let me show you 65 ter 6208. This is the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This should not be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What I'm showing you is the testimony of PW-139 in the Popovic case. And the date of the testimony is the 6th and 7th November 2006. And I'd like to refer you first to page 3672. Should be page 16 or so of this -- it is. And here you can see at lines -- just through line 15, that what this individual was talking about is about -- an event that occurred on 18th or 19th of July, 1995. And if we go to the next page, 373 [sic], you will see at line -- at line 21, he is asked the question: "May I stop you for a moment. Can I first [sic] ask you if you know approximately where this happened?" And he indicates the location of Tisova Kosa. If we go to the next page -- at the bottom of this page we can see the question: "Is this the location you believe you were captured?" And then we go to the next page, and he indicates that the area is referred to as Baljkovica. And he says that it was mentioned on a radio set the location Tisova Kosa, some 3 kilometres from Baljkovica. If we go down to the bottom of this page, we'll see that it is in private session. So I think we need to go into private session for a moment, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the Defence has nothing against admitting this PW- -- the protected witness, but it would be better for us if he were to appear here as a witness. And next, can Mr. Vanderpuye explain how were individual cases from Tisova Kosa resolved, also in Baljkovica, independent cases of execution which is, of course, good. But cases of 800, or even more, dead about which I called in 1D777, 778, 780 and 782 have not been investigated because 800 or more executed persons and their surface remains are mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Tolimir, you may deal with that during your Defence case. Mr. Vanderpuye, please continue and try to conclude your re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. If we can go over a few minutes over, hopefully I will be able to get done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, you were asked some questions about the Vragolovi grave-site at page 14.724 of the transcript. And, in particular, you were asked by General Tolimir whether the Vragolovi grave was a primary or secondary site. And in your answer, you refer to a statement by Eva Klonowski. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'd like to show you the statement by Eva Klonowski.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Going to be 65 ter 7411. Mr. President, this is yet another document which was not on the Prosecution's original 65 ter exhibit list, but, as can you see, it is directly responsive to the issues that were raised during the cross-examination concerning the Vragolovi grave-site.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, any objection to add this document to the 65 ter exhibit list?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. We have no objections to any facts that would put us in a clearer situation, all of us who are here in the courtroom. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Leave is granted to add this document to the 65 ter exhibit list. Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Here we can see the statement by Dr. Klonowski. The interview is dated 17 February 2010. I'd like to go to page 3 in the English. It's paragraph number 15. And in paragraph 15, you can see here she indicates that this was, in her opinion, a shallow primary grave, based on the position of the bodies, and so forth. Their completeness. She also indicated that if it was a secondary grave, unless the bodies were moved from the primary grave within a couple of weeks they would not have been in an anatomical order. Did you consider this, which I can see was done shortly before your report, but did you consider it in preparing your report?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And, in fact, did you refer to it specifically on page 30 of Annex A of your report, concerning the Vragolovi grave-site?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did refer to this statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'd like to tender this statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: How many pages does this witness statement to the OTP encompass?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: The statement itself, Mr. President, is -- it's two pages. With the cover page and the attachment, four. It has certain attachments that are referenced specifically in it. And the total number of pages is 105 pages, and that is because it attaches certain ICMP records concerning the individuals recovered from the -- 43 pages, I'm sorry. 43 pages. It attaches ICMP records concerning the DNA identification of the individuals found in the grave, of certain individuals found in the grave, as well as autopsy notes, notations. And she specifically refers to these in paragraph 22 of the statement. She characterised them as follows: Marked A is a sketch showing the position of the bodies that were found in the grave that she refers to, marked -- I'm sorry, that's marked B. The sketch of the site is marked A, and the documents regarding the bodies that were recovered from the site are C. And those include autopsy notes, ICMP records and so forth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, I have a problem with this procedure. To present a report -- in fact, a report by an expert witness who will not testify in this trial, by showing it -- a part of it to this witness, as a -- as an investigator of the OTP. I'm not sure if this is the best way to introduce this report into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I would first say, Mr. President, that I don't actually consider it to be a report but, in fact, a statement, but I know the rule applies just the same. But, I would point out that what it also shows is the reliability of Mr. Janc's report, and as well as substantiations the conclusions that he draws in his report. In particular, at page 30 of Annex A of his report, he says very specifically: "According to the exhumation record and to forensic anthropologist Eva Klonowski," giving the ERN of the document which I have shown the witness and the Court who was present during the exhumation, "... nine bodies were found inside the grave, DNA examinations by ICMP of human remains located within the Vragolovi grave, so far indicated the following numbers." And he has here eight identified individuals of the nine bodies that were recovered from the grave which is, of course, substantiated and corroborated by the statement of Dr. Klonowski.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, the Chamber should postpone a decision on your move to admit it into evidence --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witnesses please slow down and pause between question and answers for the benefit of the interpreters. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: My apologies. We should postpone the decision of the Chamber in relation of your move to admit this document into evidence. We have to review it, the content, to review it and the relation to the report of Mr. Janc. It was a very brief introduction, and we should only marked for identification for the moment. It will be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I have just ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter document 7411 shall be assigned Exhibit P2246, marked for identification. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, you should come to an end.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Let me just ask for 65 ter 06232.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And while that is loading, let me just ask you very quickly,

utterances.speaker: MR. JANC
utterances.text: In your report of April 2010, you indicated that eight out of the nine individuals recovered from Vragolovi have been identified.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: To your knowledge, has that changed? Has the ninth person been identified since your report?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the number is still the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Let me just show you what I have here as 65 ter 6232. On May 18th 2010, during your cross-examination you were asked by General Tolimir specifically this, "Do you consider" -- this is at page 2026 of the transcript through 2027: "Do you consider that the destruction of evidence, items found in graves, would actually prevent," and this is how it is in the transcript, "... prevent a super analysis or super expert report that would," and then it's blank, "in order to check the findings of OTP experts?" Your answer was: "Not necessarily, because if they are well preserved, and most of them are we well preserved, we have photographs of them and we have descriptions, reports on them. I don't think that would necessarily be the case. What I am showing you here is some photographs of ligatures." And we can blow it up so he can see it a little bit better. Just a few would be fine. First of all, do you recognise what I'm showing you?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, these are ligatures, photographs of ligatures which were found in mass graves.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And are these the photographs or some of the photographs you're referring to when you say that we have taken photographs of items that were found in the mass graves during the course of your cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'd like to tender this exhibit. I have a second one which I'd like to show him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Again, how many page?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: It's one page, but it features, as can you see, a number of different or discrete photographs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter document 6232 shall be assigned Exhibit P2247. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'd like to show the witness 65 ter 6233, as well, please. 6233.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, do you recognise this exhibit?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, these are photographs of blindfolds found in these mass graves.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'd also like to tend this exhibit, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter document 6233 shall be assigned Exhibit P2248. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Defence would like to know whether the two exhibits that were just admitted are in any relation to Vragolovi. Because it seems that we have some reference to other grave-sites and there is no mention of Vragolovi.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Actually, those exhibits speak to all of the items and -- recovered from all graves, in response to the cross-examination that was conducted I think I said 18th May 2010, and I indicated the transcript reference.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Last issue, Mr. Janc, and hopefully we can do this extremely fast, is: General Tolimir asked you on page 14727 through 14728 of the transcript in these proceedings on Thursday last, the following: "Was it possible in conversations with prisoners who were in Rogatica to find out who disappeared from the group of prisoners and why they didn't appear" -- and then there's some colloquy between Mr. President, the interpreter, and the accused, but he says: "... why they didn't appear at the exchange at the same time as the others who were with them at the Rasadnik prison?" And your answer was that: "Yes, there were several statements, not only of Mr. Torlak, also other individuals imprisoned in Rasadnik prison and later on exchanged were testifying or talking about these individuals." And these are individuals in the Vragolovi grave; is that right, Mr. Janc?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And: "Some of them also testified or stated that they were maltreated and beaten badly and they concluded that they were killed. Nobody actually has seen that, when and how they were killed, but they never appeared back again and they were never exchanged. And now we know where they were found. And from the exhumation records we can see that they were killed, executed." I have two questions for you. One is: During the course of your investigations, have you learned whether or not the Main Staff of the VRS was involved in the exchange process?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The Main Staff was involved in the exchange process, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And do you know if General Tolimir is indicated as having been so involved?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct. I have -- I have reviewed several documents so far with Tolimir's name on it and in relation to these issues, to the exchange of prisoners of war.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: In your review of these documents, did you ever come across a document indicating that there were certain prisoners who could be banned from being exchanged?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, first of all, this is beyond the scope of cross-examination. Second of all, perhaps we should see where the reference is where Mr. Tolimir is referred to concerning the detainees from Olovo [phoen] since the witness said he saw several such documents. Perhaps he could specify at least one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, can you give us a reference?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'm going to show Mr. Janc a document from --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: No, a reference from the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, I can. He was asked, and this is at page 14727, specifically: "Q. Thank you, Mr. Janc. You said just now that Torlak said that this and this other person said that. "Was it possible in conversation with the prisoners who ... in Rogatica to find out who disappeared from the group of prisoners and why," continuing from another point in the transcript, "why they didn't appear at the exchange at the same time as the others who were with them at the Rasadnik prison?" So my question to Mr. Janc is first: Does he know whether or not the Main Staff was involved in the exchange process, because the question was about the exchange of these prisoners. The second question is whether or not the investigation has -- he has learned in his capacity as an investigator in this case whether or not General Tolimir, himself, was involved in that exchange process. And the third thing I want to ask is about a document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, are you satisfied?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I am not. Because no document is shown which would tell us that I participated in the exchange process. It was only stated but, we need to see a document which makes direct reference to me as having participated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The first request was given by Mr. Vanderpuye, the reference to the part of the cross-examination. In relation to this specific question about the knowledge of Mr. Janc, I would agree with Mr. Tolimir, to show a document would help to clarify the situation. Otherwise, he is not the right witness to testify about these possible allegations. We are at the end of the tapes for the first session. We extended the first hearing by 20 minutes already. We should come to an end. Do you have any more questions, Mr. Vanderpuye?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I have two documents, precisely the type of documents that you'd like to see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This is not possible before the break. We must have our first break now, and we will resume at 4.35.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, I come back to the question of the -- one document we have received but only some pages of a transcript, the testimony of the witness. I would like to ask the Prosecution to upload these pages into e-court so that we can design the specific P number to that part of the transcript. You may use other parts with other witnesses, but, otherwise, it is a little bit tricky to have it confidential only in relation to this part.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. We will do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: If fact, this relates to 65 ter 06208, especially the pages 3672 through 3679. And the Registry has already assigned the number P2245, under seal, to this exhibit. Please continue, and I would kindly ask you to conclude as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I will. I have two documents I'd like to show Mr. Janc, and I'll show them both and then I'll ask him just a question or two after. The first is 65 ter 3640.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What we have here, Mr. Janc, as you can see, is a document from the security and intelligence administration from 29 May 1993. And it concerns the prisoner exchange, and it says commission work, prisoner exchange, commission's work. If we go to the last page of this document, page 2 in English, I believe, and it's page 2 in B/C/S, too. You can see that it is from General Tolimir. I indicated this is from 29 May 1993. And what it states is: "In the future, all reports on the work of the commission POW exchanges, lists of exchanged persons and persons offered for exchange shall be sent by telegram to the Republika Srpska Main Staff." And we see it's signed Chief Colonel Zdravko Tolimir. I'd like to show the next document, if I may, Mr. President. And that's 65 ter 4077.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This is not on the list of documents to be used with this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You're correct, Mr. President. The reason I've included it is because it is responsive directly to Mr. Tolimir's objection or his concerns during the course of the re-direct examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: This document, you can see, is dated 3rd September 1995. And it also concerns the exchange of prisoners and indicates that it is a report. And it refers to requests made by the commanders of the 1 KK and IVK, concerning the exchange of prisoners. And I'd like to take you to page 4 of this document. Should be -- this is the correct page in B/C/S. And here, we can see the second paragraph from the top which regards in part that: "The exchange commission chairmen must view the exchange proposal integrally, as does the Main Staff of the VRS, since, so far, the Main Staff has made the necessary number of prisoners available for the corps commissions in circumstances where they did not have a sufficient number of captured enemy soldiers to exchange for all the captured members of their corps." And then it says: "Security organs and exchange commission chairmen must also avoid using parents' bitterness because it is not possible to exchange prisoners who have been in prison for quite some time, particularly because the VRS Main Staff is not responsible for this situation, rather, it is the result of the small number of enemy soldiers captured by our units." If we go to the last page and on the bottom of the page in the B/C/S, we can see that this comes from General Tolimir, Assistant Commander. I have two questions, Mr. Janc. The first is: Do these documents show, as you've testified, the involvement of General Tolimir and the Main Staff in the prisoner exchange process?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I just have an objection to the fact that Mr. Vanderpuye and the witness said that I participated in the exchange of prisoners from Vragolovi. And I was not in Republika Srpska even theoretically at the time, but I will not testify. But, please, can Mr. Vanderpuye clarify whether a document from 1993 and a document about the exchange from 1995, which relate to the 1st and 2nd Corps, can -- have to do with Vragolovi and the exchange which took place in Vragolovi in January of 1996. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I think my question was very clear from the beginning, and I believe I asked it before we broke, which was: In response to Mr. Tolimir's questioning of Mr. Janc on cross-examination as to why it is that certain prisoners at Vragolovi did not appear for exchange, I asked Mr. Janc if he was aware if the Main Staff was involved in the exchange of prisoners and whether or not General Tolimir was involved in the exchange of prisoners. And he indicated that the answer was yes. That's the reason why I'm showing him these documents, to confirm the basis of his knowledge or the source of his information reaching that conclusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I have some problem to understand why you are putting these questions to Mr. Janc, as an investigator of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'm putting them to Mr. Janc, Mr. President, because General Tolimir put to Mr. Janc the question of why it is that certain prisoners didn't show up for exchange. And that can be found in the transcript at 14727 through 14728. Where he specifically asked him: Was it possible -- was it possible to find out why they didn't appear at the exchange at the same time as the others who were with them in the Rasadnik prison. So my question is whether or not Mr. Janc is aware if the Main Staff was involved in the exchange process, I think is how I characterised it almost verbatim, which doesn't necessarily have to do with Rasadnik prison or Vragolovi grave, particularly, but with the process of exchange of prisoners, and, by that, I mean all prisoners which is what I think these documents demonstrate and I've put to Mr. Janc.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, do you have any knowledge about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, I can confirm that I have seen and reviewed these two documents along with many, many others, which relate to the same topic and are signed by General Tolimir. So I can say that he -- the Main Staff and, particularly, General Tolimir was involved in this exchange process.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Your knowledge is based on these documents that we have seen today in the courtroom; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Also on these two documents but not only on these two documents. There are many, many others, especially from December 1995 and January 1996.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And you are referring to other documents, or do you have other sources for this information?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm referring now mostly, and I think exclusively to documents, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I would tender the two documents I've shown Mr. Janc. If this is still -- if this is an issue for the Court, I have other documents I can show him as well. The two documents I showed were 65 ter 3640 and 4077, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Do you have any objections, Mr. Tolimir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no objection, Mr. President. I do not distance myself at all from any activities of the Main Staff. I'm just saying that in January 1996 when the exchange about which the witness was saying, that that is something I did not participate in. This is why I requested that a document be shown which shows that I did not take part in this. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: As there is no objection, both documents will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter document 3640 shall be assigned Exhibit P2249. And the 65 ter document 4077 shall be assigned Exhibit P2250. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I can show Mr. Janc one other document at 4088 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You wanted to show two documents. You have done that already.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. I have no problem resting at this point, but I understand that General Tolimir has an issue as concerns his involvement in the prisoner exchange process. Mr. Janc has referred to documents from December of 1995, and I have one such document I can show him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: It's 65 ter 4088.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: This is a document, Mr. Janc, from 15 December 1995 also from the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If we go to the next page in the B/C/S, we will see that this document is from General Tolimir. And if we go to item number 1 on this document, on the first page. Item number 1 is at the bottom, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And it reads that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Is there an English translation?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I believe there is. I'm looking at one, but I'm not sure if it is uploaded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I was told it was not uploaded.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I will read this part of the document, and maybe we can marked for identification, pending translation. It reads just above item number 1, it talks about the implementation of an exchange. And then item 1 says: "From 0800 hours on 16 December 1995, send lists of people from our prisons whom we can offer to be exchanged to the Main Staff, General Tolimir, personally."

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Again, Mr. Janc, my question is: Is this one of the documents that you have relied on or that you have reviewed and/or relied on in reaching the conclusion that you have concerning General Tolimir's involvement in the prisoner exchange process?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would tender this last exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: No objection, Mr. Tolimir?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. No, Mr. President. I'm just saying that I did not take part in the exchange on the 18th of January, 1996, about which Mr. Vanderpuye has been talking. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Since there is, again, no objection, this will be marked for identification, pending translation.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, 65 ter document 4088 shall be assigned Exhibit P2251, marked for identification, pending translation. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: That concludes my re-direct examination, Mr. President. I appreciate your indulgence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, you will be pleased to hear that this concludes your testimony in this trial. You have been quite often in this courtroom and in this trial testifying here. The Chamber would like to thank you that you were able to come here and to provide us with your knowledge. Now you are free to return to your normal activities, and there is no limitation of your contact to your colleagues in the OTP any longer. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, is the next witness ready.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I understand that he is ready, Mr. President. There is one other issue, though; and that is, in relation to Mr. Janc's testimony, we did also plan to call him in relation to some intercept evidence which I think is also part of his 65 ter summary and in the application that we had to re-call him, but we will have to schedule that for some other time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. The next witness should be brought in, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Elderkin. Welcome to the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Your Honours, good afternoon. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir. Welcome to the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Would you please read aloud the affirmation on the card which is shown to you now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please sit down and make yourself comfortable. Mr. Elderkin for the Prosecution is now conducting the examination-in-chief. Mr. Elderkin.
